## Start with the problemyou have today

Pick the one that sounds like your week, and see how we fixed it for other teams.

### Your engineers spend too much time on infrastructure upkeep

Cast AI rightsizes workloads, provisions nodes from your node templates, and
consolidates underused ones, all within the policies you set. When a fix
belongs in code, such as Helm values or Terraform, it opens a pull request for
your team to review.

[See Kubernetes automation in action](https://cast.ai/#story-panel)

### You pay for capacity your workloads never use

Cast AI sets each workload’s CPU and memory requests from observed usage, then
bin-packs pods onto fewer, better-fitting nodes and moves eligible workloads
to spot instances. Your node count follows real demand instead of peak
requests.

[See how cost optimization works](https://cast.ai/kubernetes-cost-optimization/)

### The GPUs you need aren't available where you run

When your region runs out of GPUs, Cast AI provisions nodes in other clouds
and regions through OMNI Compute and schedules eligible workloads there, while
your control plane stays in your current cluster. For GPUs you already have,
time-slicing and MIG let several workloads share one device.

[Learn about cross-cloud GPUs](https://cast.ai/cross-cloud-gpu-access/)

### Your database is slow and overloaded

Cast AI’s Database Optimizer sits in front of PostgreSQL and MySQL. It caches
repeated reads, pools connections so traffic spikes don’t exhaust your
connection limit, and flags slow queries with suggested fixes.

[Learn about Database Optimizer](https://cast.ai/database-optimization/)

## Cast AI observes, decides, and acts

It reads how your workloads and nodes behave, works out what should change, and
applies eligible changes to live infrastructure within your policies. When a change
belongs in your repo, it opens a pull request for your team to review.

Observe and decide

### Workloads and nodes, tuned together

Workload rightsizing informs node capacity, bin-packing, and placement. Node
conditions and available capacity inform workload adjustments and remediation.
Cast AI connects both while preserving existing policies and integrations.

Keep your existing Cluster Autoscaler, Karpenter or use Cast AI's native
autoscaler.
